subject: biology
promptStrong: Give me a 6-mark exam-style question on {lo} for {board} {level} {subject}, then mark my answer against the mark scheme.
promptWeak: Explain {lo} for {board} {level} {subject} simply, with a worked example and the most common mistake students make.

questions.q: Which statement about enzymes after they catalyse a reaction is correct?
options: They are permanently changed into the product
They are used up and must be remade
They are unchanged and can be reused
questions.explain: As catalysts, enzymes are not used up and can catalyse further reactions.

questions.q: Why do palisade cells near the top of a leaf contain many chloroplasts?
options: To absorb maximum light for photosynthesis
questions.explain: Palisade mesophyll cells are packed with chloroplasts to capture as much light as possible.

questions.q: Bile is stored in which organ before release into the small intestine?
questions.explain: Bile made in the liver is stored in the gall bladder until needed.

questions.q: What is the role of fibre in a balanced diet?
options: Helps food move through the gut and prevents constipation
questions.explain: Dietary fibre is not digested but keeps food moving through the intestines.

questions.q: In the emulsion (ethanol) test, a positive result for lipids is:
questions.explain: Adding ethanol then water to a lipid produces a cloudy white emulsion.

questions.q: Why is a plant often kept in the dark before testing a leaf for starch?
options: To destarch the leaf so any new starch comes from the experiment
questions.explain: Destarching ensures any starch found afterwards was made during the test conditions.

questions.q: Which food test uses Benedict's solution, and what positive result shows?
options: Test for lipid; forms a milky emulsion
Test for sugar (reducing sugar); turns from blue to brick-red/orange on heating
questions.explain: Benedict's solution, heated, turns from blue to brick-red/orange when a reducing sugar is present.

questions.q: Why do single-celled organisms NOT need a transport system?
options: They use active transport for everything
They have a large surface area to volume ratio so diffusion is sufficient
questions.explain: Their large surface area to volume ratio and short diffusion distances allow exchange by diffusion alone.

questions.q: Why does each enzyme only catalyse one type of reaction?
options: Each enzyme is used up after one reaction
Enzymes only work at one temperature in the whole body
The active site is a specific shape that only fits one substrate
questions.explain: Enzyme specificity comes from the specific shape of the active site, which fits only its complementary substrate.

questions.q: Root hair cells are well adapted for absorbing water because they:
options: Carry out active transport of water
Have a large surface area and a thin cell wall
questions.explain: A large surface area and thin wall maximise water uptake by osmosis (water is never moved by active transport).

questions.q: Why does the rate of photosynthesis eventually level off as light intensity keeps increasing?
options: Another factor such as CO2 or temperature becomes limiting
questions.explain: At high light, another factor (CO2 or temperature) limits the rate, so it plateaus.

questions.q: Plant roots absorb mineral ions from very dilute soil solutions by active transport because:
options: The ions move down their concentration gradient
The ions must be moved against the concentration gradient into the root
The ion concentration is higher in the soil than in the root
questions.explain: Mineral ions are usually more concentrated inside the root, so they must be moved against the gradient by active transport.
